Amazon plans a $100 million-plus factory to support its robotics network

The Greenwood, Indiana facility will combine fabrication, robotic welding, coating and assembly, with a planned 2028 launch and 300 jobs.

The Robot Report ↗25 September 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 1Videos 1

A factory for the fulfillment network

Amazon announced on September 24 that it plans to invest more than $100 million in a roughly 585,000-square-foot advanced manufacturing facility in Greenwood, Indiana. It will supply the North American fulfillment and robotics network, with a launch expected by 2028.

Several processes under one roof

Planned capabilities include fabrication, robotic welding, automated powder coating and assembly, supported by AWS, AI manufacturing systems and robotics. The announcement does not identify a particular robot model that the facility will manufacture.

Manufacturing and engineering jobs

Amazon expects 300 manufacturing and engineering positions, including CNC operators, welders, coating technicians, assemblers and controls engineers. The project combines automation investment with the people needed to operate and maintain production.

An announced investment, not an operating plant

The facility and opening date remain plans. The accompanying images and video illustrate Amazon’s existing robotics work. The Indiana project is separate from the Texas manufacturing investment announced earlier.
